# bench_replay on session.itch

Generated by `scripts/bench_driver.py` from raw records that are not committed. Do not edit by hand.

Host: **macOS (M4 Max)**. Numbers from the two hosts are never mixed.

**macOS (M4 Max) is not a pinned host.** macOS offers no way to pin a thread, so each process ran wherever the scheduler put it, beside whatever else the machine was doing under `measure.sh`'s lock. Every figure here is a macOS figure, and a bar set on x86 Linux is not passed or failed by one.

## Summary

Each repetition is a fresh process: one warm-up pass, excluded from every figure here, then a throughput pass on a fresh book, with no latency pass, and a second process for the untimed pass of counters and memory. Every design of the run ran in each repetition, one after the other. 3 repetitions.

The mean service time is the throughput pass's time over every message, frame walk included (T-LAT-3). The batch mean is the same time over the 3,312 book messages, carteret's denominator: `A`, `F`, `E`, `C`, `X`, `D`, `U`, `P` and `Q` (T-LAT-4).

| Figure | Median | Min | Max | CV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput, messages/s | 17,775,764 | 17,568,696 | 18,517,146 | 2.78% |
| Mean service time per message, ns | 56.16 | 54.05 | 57.06 | 2.76% |
| Batch mean per book message, ns | 56.46 | 54.35 | 57.37 | 2.76% |
| Book memory, MiB | 3.2 | 3.2 | 3.2 | 0.85% |

## Latency

Not measured: this design ran no latency pass in this run, as `passes` in the header says, so no latency figure is published for it.

## How this run reads the day

The day was read into anonymous memory before the warm-up and never mapped, so each pass reads a copy in RAM. Nothing read the top of book: each pass timed the book alone. This is itch-book's T-BOOK-1 method: its book_throughput reads the whole file into a buffer and times the book alone, with no top-of-book work.

## Per-operation latency

Not measured: this design ran no latency pass in this run, as `passes` in the header says, so no per-operation latency figure is published for it.

## Book memory

T-BOOK-3. Read from phys_footprint from task_info(TASK_VM_INFO), in a process of its own that builds no other book first: once before the book is built, once after, every 1,048,576 messages of the untimed pass and at its end. The book's memory is the most charged at any reading less the reading before it was built. That is what the book itself takes, not the mapped file or the input copy, which are in the first reading, and not the latency samples, which that process never makes. itch-book's figure is peak RSS less the input buffer, the same quantity read another way.

| Figure | Median | Min | Max | CV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Book memory, MiB | 3.2 | 3.2 | 3.2 | 0.85% |
| Charged before the book was built, MiB | 1.4 | 1.4 | 1.4 | 0.64% |
| Charged once it was built, before any message, MiB | 4.4 | 4.4 | 4.4 | 0.20% |
| Charged at the most, MiB | 4.6 | 4.6 | 4.6 | 0.39% |
